items.title: EBA Founder Eniola Omoniyi Calls for More Strategic Brand Building Following NAC 2026 - THISDAYLIVE
items.raw_summary: Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google Follow us on Google Eniola Omoniyi, popularly known as Eniivy and Iyalode, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of ENI Brand Architect Limited (EBA), has emphasised the need for businesses and marketing communications agencies to move beyond brand visibility and focus on strategy, credibility and measurable business outcomes. Reflecting on discussions at the 2026 National Advertising Conference (NAC) in Abuja, Eniola noted that the changing expectations of consumers and businesses require a broader approach to brand building and marketing communications. The conference, themed “Repositioning the Marketing Communications Industry for the Next Frontier,” brought together advertising professionals, business leaders, regulators and other industry stakeholders to examine the future of Nigeria’s marketing communications industry. For Eniola, one of the important conversations emerging from the conference is the distinction between attracting attention and building a business that can sustain consumer trust. “Visibility gets people to notice your brand, but credibility gives them a reason to trust it. Businesses must understand that being seen is different from being chosen. A successful campaign can attract attention, but what happens after that attention is what determines whether people become customers and whether those customers return,” she said. She explained that businesses must pay greater attention to the relationship between brand promises, customer experience and actual service delivery. According to her, a business can invest significantly in advertising, public relations and digital marketing, but those investments may deliver limited long-term value if its positioning is unclear or the customer experience contradicts its communication. Eniola also highlighted the changing responsibilities of marketing communications agencies, noting that businesses increasingly require partners who understand their commercial objectives and can contribute to solving problems beyond promotional activities. “An agency should be able to ask what problem a business is trying to solve, who it is trying to reach, what needs to change and how success will be measured. We have to move beyond simply delivering campaigns and start paying closer attention to the business objectives those campaigns are expected to achieve,” she added. As Founder and CEO of ENI Brand Architect, a company providing integrated business strategy, brand development, communications, creative production and execution services, Eniola’s perspective draws from working with organisationsacross different sectors and stages of business development. Her experience also extends to broadcasting, event production, partnerships and community engagement. She serves as Head of Events and Sponsorships at Lounge Network and is the convener of The Eniivy Experience, a community platform established in 2018. Drawing from these experiences, she identified strategic positioning, consumer understanding, consistency and adaptability as important considerations for businesses seeking sustainable growth. She noted that brands must understand the people they serve, remain consistent in their promises and delivery, and adapt to changing market conditions without losing the identity that makes them recognisable. For communications agencies, Eniola believes the industry’s next stage of development will require stronger business understanding, greater accountability and a willingness to challenge approaches that prioritise activity over outcomes. Reflecting on NAC 2026, she maintained that repositioning Nigeria’s marketing communications industry should extend beyond conversations about emerging technologies, new platforms and changing consumer behaviour. It must also influence how businesses define their objectives, how agencies develop solutions and how success is evaluated. For Eniola, the future of brand building lies in connecting strategy with execution and ensuring that every communication effort contributes to a clear business purpose.

items.title: Too Handsome To Ignore, But Is H.I.M Built To Last? - BW Marketing World
items.raw_summary: Actor Ranveer Singh and entrepreneur Aman Gupta’s H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man) enters the men’s personal care category with an unapologetic name, a founder story rooted in an unusual compliment and a proposition centred on Indian men’s grooming needs.The brand takes its cue from a remark Singh says a basketball player at an NBA game in the US told him: “You’re too handsome for an Indian man.” The founders turn the remark into a larger brand idea celebrating Indian masculinity, appearance and confidence.The launch film, ‘Tested On Ranveer Singh’, takes viewers behind the making of H.I.M, blending humour, science and grooming while positioning Singh as a co-founder and product participant rather than merely a celebrity endorser.What WorkedTurning a comment into a brand ideaThe origin story is the campaign’s strongest creative hook. “Too handsome for an Indian man” remark could have been dismissed as a throwaway compliment, but the brand turns it into a statement about confidence and Indian identity.The name H.I.M. is memorable, bold and conversation-worthy. It gives the brand a cultural entry point instead of starting with a conventional product-benefit pitch, while opening up a broader conversation around Indian masculinity and grooming.What's in a name?The name H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man) is striking, bold and instantly memorable. It stands out in a category often dominated by conventional, functional brand names, giving the brand a distinct identity and an easy conversation starter.Ranveer Singh as co-founder, not just celebrityThe ‘Tested On Ranveer Singh’ campaign’s credibility lever is Singh’s positioning as a co-founder and product participant. According to the brand, he tested more than 100 formulations, insisted on testing shampoo in Indian hard water and wanted face cream tested in heat and humidity rather than just air-conditioned laboratories.Singh’s involvement, from product development to packaging and naming the proprietary molecule IN·XT™, reinforces the narrative of a celebrity invested in building the business. For a category crowded with endorsements, this gives the partnership a more substantive reason to exist.Humour and science give the brand personalityMen’s personal care advertising often relies on predictable codes of muscularity, attractiveness and confidence. H.I.M’s irreverent positioning offers an opportunity to play with these conventions. Its humour, rooted in familiar Indian grooming behaviours, makes the brand relatable rather than aspirational in a conventional sense.The science-led proposition also adds substance. With eight products across face, body and hair, formulated for Indian skin, climate and biology, H.I.M connects its IN·XT technology to conditions such as hard water, heat and humidity. This makes the innovation story more relevant to consumers’ everyday experiences.A launch designed for creator participationThe creator-first launch was a smart extension of the brand’s audience strategy. Bringing together creators from fashion, comedy, music and fitness, alongside product trial stations, shower-thoughts recordings and fit-check mirrors, turned the event into a content-generating experience rather than just a launch venue.What Could Have Been StrongerThe brand risks being overshadowed by its foundersRanveer Singh’s personality, the origin anecdote and the celebrity-founder narrative are likely to be the campaign’s strongest recall drivers. The challenge is whether consumers will remember H.I.M as a distinct brand or primarily as Ranveer Singh and Aman Gupta’s venture. Celebrity-led awareness does not automatically translate into consideration, trial or repeat purchase.The product proposition needs to compete with the entertainmentThe storytelling makes for an engaging launch, but personal care purchase decisions ultimately rest on efficacy, price, convenience and trust. The campaign needs to clearly establish what makes H.I.M different, what IN·XT delivers and why consumers should switch from products they already use.The positioning needs to go beyond handsomeThe name is provocative and memorable, but the brand will need to build a broader narrative around grooming, self-care, confidence and individuality. If H.I.M wants to speak to the evolved Indian man, its communication must extend beyond physical appearance and embrace diverse identities and grooming habits.The VerdictH.I.M is attempting to build a brand at the intersection of celebrity, culture, entrepreneurship and product science. Its launch makes the brand feel like a conversation rather than a conventional grooming campaign. The name is memorable, the origin story is intriguing, and Singh’s reported involvement adds credibility.But the real test begins after the launch buzz. Can H.I.M turn personality into preference, science into trust, and attention into repeat purchase?H.I.M has made an attention-grabbing entrance. Now it needs to turn attention into a brand consumers believe in, buy and return to.

items.title: Spotlight Promotions: Delhi-Based Digital Marketing and Social Media Marketing Agency Led by Brijesh Dhingra and Sugandha Aneja Dhingra - https://www.indiagazette.com/
items.raw_summary: Spotlight Promotions, a Delhi-based digital marketing agency and social media marketing agency specialising in the restaurant, hospitality and food and beverage (F&B) industry, is strengthening its presence in India's growing digital marketing landscape under the leadership of Founder Brijesh Dhingra and Co-Founder Sugandha Aneja Dhingra. With expertise in restaurant marketing, hospitality branding and digital brand development, Spotlight Promotions has successfully handled more than 300 projects and currently manages approximately 100 active clients. Positioned as a specialised hospitality marketing agency, the company provides a comprehensive range of services, including social media management, digital marketing, brand strategy, restaurant branding, creative campaign development, professional food photography, videography, influencer marketing coordination, digital promotions and restaurant launch marketing. Founded with the vision of helping businesses build distinctive brand identities, Spotlight Promotions focuses on delivering integrated digital marketing solutions for restaurants, cafes, lounges, clubs, premium dining destinations and hospitality businesses. The agency has worked with several recognised names in the hospitality and entertainment industry, including Studio XO, Molecule and Cafe Delhi Heights. Its approach combines creative storytelling, strategic social media marketing and professional visual content to help brands establish a stronger digital presence. Brijesh Dhingra, Founder of Spotlight Promotions, has been instrumental in shaping the company's business vision, client relationships and expansion within the digital marketing and hospitality sectors. His approach focuses on understanding the unique positioning of each business and developing customised marketing strategies that support brand awareness, customer engagement and business growth. Sugandha Aneja Dhingra, Co-Founder of Spotlight Promotions, plays an important role in the company's leadership and development. Together, the founders are building a digital marketing agency focused on creative excellence, strategic execution and long-term brand partnerships. One of the company's key specialisations is restaurant digital marketing. Its services cover the complete marketing journey of a hospitality brand, from initial brand development and restaurant branding to professional food shoots, social media management, promotional campaigns and launch strategies. As a full-service social media marketing agency, Spotlight Promotions also works on Instagram marketing, Facebook marketing, content creation, reels production, creative design, audience engagement and digital brand positioning. The company aims to help hospitality businesses communicate their identity effectively and maintain a consistent presence across digital platforms. Speaking about the company's vision, Brijesh Dhingra said, "Our objective has always been to go beyond conventional social media management. We believe every hospitality brand has its own identity, story and audience. Our focus is to understand that individuality and build marketing strategies that reflect the brand's vision while creating a strong market presence." With more than 300 completed projects and approximately 100 active clients, Spotlight Promotions continues to expand its footprint as a digital marketing agency in Delhi, with a specialised focus on restaurant marketing, social media management and hospitality brand development. As India's hospitality industry becomes increasingly competitive and digitally driven, Spotlight Promotions aims to strengthen its position as a trusted marketing partner for restaurants and hospitality brands through strategic thinking, creative execution and integrated digital marketing solutions. https
